sense: a striking difference between things set side by side

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.57: sī contentiō quaedam et comparātiō fīat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Setting one thing against another, in thought or in words; in rhetoric, antithesis (Lewis & Short). Not the plain word: its first senses are straining, effort and dispute. Most often Latin shows a contrast by setting two clauses side by side (see whereas) or by comparing (see compare); for the unlikeness itself see difference (dissimilitūdō).

terms.gloss: by contrast, on the other hand
evidence: Pac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.36: sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “on the contrary, on the other hand, vice versā; sometimes almost = sed or autem”. As a preposition with the accusative, against, opposite.

phrases.latin: sī contentiō quaedam et comparātiō fīat
phrases.english: if a contrast and comparison of some kind were made

phrases.latin: fortūnam īnsānam esse … perhibent philosophī … sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre
phrases.english: philosophers say that fortune is mad … but there are other philosophers who, by contrast, deny that there is any such thing as Fortune

sources: Lewis & Short: contentio · Lewis & Short: contra
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
